title: Bipedal3Matrix column-major + transpose tests
description:
Implement `Bipedal3Matrix` in column-major layout (per the R3 design SSOT) with row/column accessors and transpose tests.

## Background

The R3 multi-word streaming column-sum design (issue `60c30e2d`) chose column-major layout for `Bipedal3Matrix` because Ryser's inner loop walks down a column at each Gray-code step. Storing matrices column-major aligns each column with a contiguous `Bipedal3Vec`, which the streaming inner loop processes word-at-a-time without strided access.

This is the SSOT layout choice for the entire epic. T7's generic `permanent_ryser` and T9's `permanent_bipedal3` both consume this layout.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] [hard] `Bipedal3Matrix` stores rows × cols as a single `Bipedal3Vec` per column (column-major).
- [ ] [hard] Constructor from a row-major `&[Fp<3>]` slice exists, plus the inverse round-trip accessor (lane-by-lane decode to row-major).
- [ ] [hard] `column(i) -> &Bipedal3Vec` and `row(i) -> Bipedal3Vec` accessors exist; row access reconstructs by gather-decode.
- [ ] [hard] Transpose round-trip: `M.transpose().transpose()` is bit-equal to `M` on 100 random matrices for shapes covering rectangular non-multiples-of-64.
- [ ] [hard] Word-boundary tests cover dimensions where rows or cols hit {1, 63, 64, 65}.
- [ ] [hard] `cargo nextest run -p gf2-algebra --release --profile ci` passes.
